passages.text: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise.
This promise is that people can enter His rest.
This promise still remains.
We must be careful.
None of you should be found to have missed this promise.
We must not fall short of entering God’s rest.
passages.original: Φοβηθῶμεν οὖν μή‿ ποτε καταλειπομένης ἐπαγγελίας εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ δοκῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ὑστερηκέναι

passages.text: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.
passages.sermon:
We received the good news.
They also received the good news.
The message they heard did not help them.
They did not join the message with faith.
Only those who had faith benefited from the message.
passages.original: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους μὴ συγκεκερασμένους τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν

passages.text: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.
passages.sermon: We who have believed enter God's rest.\r\nGod said, “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”\r\nGod finished His works since the foundation of the world.
passages.original: Εἰσερχόμεθα γὰρ εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν οἱ πιστεύσαντες καθὼς εἴρηκεν Ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου Καίτοι τῶν ἔργων ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου γενηθέντων

passages.text: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the seventh day.
He said this in Scripture.
God rested on the seventh day.
He stopped all His works on that day.
passages.original: εἴρηκεν γάρ που περὶ τῆς ἑβδόμης οὕτως Καὶ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke earlier about His rest.
He said, “They shall never enter My rest.”
God repeats this warning again here.
He says, “They shall never enter My rest.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου

passages.text: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience, God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
passages.sermon:
God offers rest to His people.
Some people have not yet entered this rest.
God gave the good news to people in the past.
These people did not enter God's rest.
They did not enter because they disobeyed God.
God chose another day for entering His rest.
God called this day “Today.”
God spoke through David after a long time.
God said, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
passages.original: Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἀπολείπεται τινὰς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς αὐτήν καὶ οἱ πρότερον εὐαγγελισθέντες οὐκ εἰσῆλθον δι’ ἀπείθειαν πάλιν τινὰ ὁρίζει ἡμέραν Σήμερον ἐν Δαυὶδ λέγων μετὰ τοσοῦτον χρόνον καθὼς προείρηται Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν

passages.text: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was a leader of Israel after Moses.
Joshua led the people into the promised land.
Joshua did not give the people final rest.
God spoke about another day of rest after Joshua’s time.
If Joshua had given them true rest, God would not have spoken about another day.
God’s promise of rest continued after Joshua.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ αὐτοὺς Ἰησοῦς κατέπαυσεν οὐκ ἂν περὶ ἄλλης ἐλάλει μετὰ ταῦτα ἡμέρας

passages.text: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
passages.sermon:
God gives rest to His people.
This rest is like a Sabbath.
This Sabbath rest still remains for God’s people.
God’s people can enter this rest.
passages.original: ἄρα ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμὸς τῷ λαῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.
passages.sermon:
God rested from His own work.
Whoever enters God’s rest also stops working.
This person rests from his own work.
He rests in the same way that God rested.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.
passages.sermon:
God promises rest to His people.
This rest is like the Sabbath rest.
Let us try hard to enter this rest.
We must not follow the example of those who disobeyed.
If we follow their example, we will fall as they did.
passages.original: Σπουδάσωμεν οὖν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν κατάπαυσιν ἵνα μὴ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ τις ὑποδείγματι πέσῃ τῆς ἀπειθείας

passages.text: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
passages.sermon:
The word of God is living.
The word of God is active.
The word of God is sharper than any double-edged sword.
The word of God pierces deeply.
It divides soul and spirit.
It divides joints and marrow.
The word of God judges the thoughts of the heart.
It judges the intentions of the heart.
passages.original: Ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐνεργὴς καὶ τομώτερος ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον καὶ διϊκνούμενος ἄχρι μερισμοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ πνεύματος ἁρμῶν τε καὶ μυελῶν καὶ κριτικὸς ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας

passages.text: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.
passages.sermon:
God sees everything in creation.
Nothing is hidden from God.
Everything is uncovered before God’s eyes.
Everything is exposed to God.
We must give account to God.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν κτίσις ἀφανὴς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πάντα δὲ γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος

passages.text: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus is our great high priest.
Jesus has passed through the heavens.
We have this high priest.
Let us hold firmly to what we believe.
passages.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν ἀρχιερέα μέγαν διεληλυθότα τοὺς οὐρανούς Ἰησοῦν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ κρατῶμεν τῆς ὁμολογίας

passages.text: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our high priest.
He is the Son of God.
Jesus can sympathize with our weaknesses.
He was tempted in every way, just as we are.
Jesus did not sin.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα μὴ δυνάμενον συμπαθῆσαι ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ἡμῶν πεπειρασμένον δὲ κατὰ πάντα καθ’ ὁμοιότητα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is our great high priest.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus has passed through the heavens.
We can approach the throne of grace.
We should come with confidence.
We will receive mercy.
We will find grace.
Grace will help us when we need it.
passages.original: προσερχώμεθα οὖν μετὰ παρρησίας τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος ἵνα λάβωμεν ἔλεος καὶ χάριν εὕρωμεν εἰς εὔκαιρον βοήθειαν
